evidence: The redundant `store` param let a caller pass a value that diverged from `binding.store()`; the fix drops the param and calls `binding.store()` internally, removing the two-sources risk the reviewer named.
guidance_note: Don't add a parameter for state already reachable off the primary argument; take it from the source object directly.

evidence: `toLegacyCell` reimplemented `toStripCell`'s padding/style logic by hand; the fix routes `legacySegmentBytes` through the real `buildLineStrip` with a stub, deleting the parallel implementation so there is nothing left to drift.
guidance_note: When writing a parity/test harness, render through the same production function the code under test uses, rather than hand-copying its logic into a helper.

evidence: Verified in the repo at 53dce2f: tsconfig.json excludes "test" and jest.config.js sets extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts'], which is consistent with the agent's claim that neither `import.meta.url` (needs esnext module for type-check) nor `__dirname` (undefined under native ESM) works in test files, and `pnpm test` always runs from the package root so process.cwd() is stable in practice. The general concern (cwd-dependent paths are fragile) is real but the suggested fix was not viable in this toolchain.

Reviewer asked for `satisfies Record<SegmentName, SegmentParityEntry>`; the agent instead used a plain `Record<SegmentName, SegmentParityEntry>` annotation because `satisfies` collapsed every entry's `status` to the literal "legacy-only" and dropped the optional `dsl` field, breaking later dsl-parity entries. A plain annotation gets the same exhaustiveness (missing/extra key is a compile error) while keeping the wide element type — a correct and necessary deviation from the letter of the suggestion.
guidance_note: When adding compile-time exhaustiveness to a Record literal whose values vary in shape across keys, check whether `satisfies` over-narrows the literal before defaulting to it.

evidence: The agent exported `SegmentName` (satisfying the compile-time-safety half of the ask) but declined to narrow `VALID_SEGMENT_NAMES` to `ReadonlySet<SegmentName>`, since its sole caller passes an untrusted CLI string and `ReadonlySet<SegmentName>.has()` requires an argument assignable to `SegmentName` — narrowing would force an `as SegmentName` cast at exactly the validation boundary meant to reject bad input. This is correct TypeScript Set-typing behavior, not a rationalization.
guidance_note: When a validated boundary takes untrusted string input, keep the container type at that boundary as `string` and export the narrow union separately for already-typed consumers.

evidence: `gh api repos/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits/5bf997c` shows it touched only src/config/loader.ts and test/parity/registry.ts (the F4/F5 fix); the dslSegmentBytes truthiness code in harness.ts this finding targets is unchanged from the original round-0 diff (a483ac3). The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive here: this is an original-PR gap the reviewer caught one round late, not something the F4/F5 fix caused.
guidance_note: Distinguish 'unset' from 'explicit empty string' with `!== undefined` for optional string config fields from the start, so invalid config fails loudly instead of being silently treated as absent.

evidence: The 5bf997c patch for registry.ts (checked via gh) only added an import and changed PARITY_REGISTRY's type annotation; it did not touch the `SegmentParityEntry.dsl` field or its comment, which is verbatim from the original round-0 diff shown under F4. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the stale comment predates 5bf997c.
guidance_note: Write a doc-comment describing status-gated behavior to match the actual condition in the code at authoring time, not an aspirational future condition.

evidence: 5bf997c's file list (via gh) is only src/config/loader.ts and test/parity/registry.ts — it never touched test/parity.test.ts, so the unused `SegmentBytes` import predates 5bf997c and is unrelated to the F4/F5 fix. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive here.
guidance_note: Check for unused type-only imports before pushing a new test file that imports several types from the same module.

narrative: A parity-harness PR where every finding but one pushback was a real, distinct issue; the round-1 findings (F6-F8) all landed on the commit that carried the F4/F5 fix but were, on inspection of the actual diffs, pre-existing round-0 gaps the reviewer simply hadn't caught yet, not regressions from that fix. The agent's two pushbacks (F3, and half of F5) were grounded in verifiable toolchain and type-system constraints rather than preference, and neither was contradicted in later rounds.
guidance_observations: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag fired three times in this PR without any of the three actually being caused by the named fix — commit-adjacency is not evidence of causation, only diffing the named commit settles it.
Both pushbacks cited concrete, checkable facts (a tsconfig exclusion, a Set<T> typing rule) rather than a bare law token, and held up under verification.

evidence: coalescePlainRun dropped bgcolor entirely for multi-fragment runs, exactly matching the reviewer's onBlue+onBlue example. The fix re-derives the coalescing rule from rich-js's actual single-style-per-cell invariant (split on bgcolor boundary) instead of the assumed 'one run = one cell' rule, and adds two tests (shared-bg preserved, bg-change splits) covering the reported case.
guidance_note: When a merge/coalesce operation has to respect a downstream single-value-per-unit constraint (here: one bgcolor per StripCell), derive the coalescing boundary from that constraint before writing the loop, not after a reviewer finds the drop.

evidence: The original test asserted only the visible text and would have passed even if the styled fragment were silently flattened to plain. The fix renders the cells to truecolor ANSI and asserts an SGR escape is present plus the escape-stripped text is exactly right, so a flatten-to-plain regression would now fail the test.
guidance_note: When a test claims 'styling is preserved', assert on the rendered/observable output (e.g. an ANSI escape is present) rather than only on derived text equality.

narrative: A small, focused fix PR: both Copilot findings named real bugs (a silent style drop and a vacuous test), and the agent's fixes addressed the actual root cause in each case rather than patching the symptom, closing the PR in two rounds with no follow-on findings.
guidance_observations: Both findings were accepted and root-caused on the first reply with no pushback and no partial fixes — the cleanest PR in this batch.

evidence: DSL_BINDINGS' `Partial<Record<...>>` annotation widened known keys to `DslBinding | undefined`, and the harness only checks `dsl !== undefined` at runtime — so a dsl-parity entry that got `undefined` would silently skip its byte-parity assertion, a real false-green risk. `satisfies` closes exactly that gap by keeping referenced keys non-optional.
guidance_note: Use `satisfies <Constraint>` on a config/registry literal that needs compile-time-checked completeness from its first commit, not only after a reviewer flags the gap.

evidence: Confirmed via `gh api .../commits/298bc53`: that commit's only change was adding `satisfies Partial<Record<SegmentName, DslBinding>>` to the DSL_BINDINGS declaration; it did not touch the env binding. The missing `when` guard (env always rendering, unlike legacy's null-on-falsy) is present verbatim in the original round-0 commit b434ef7. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation here — this is an original gap, first caught in round 1.
guidance_note: Port every 'returns null when X' branch of a migrated renderer into a `when` guard on the segment's first DSL declaration, for every segment being migrated, not only the ones a reviewer flags.

evidence: Confirmed via gh that 298bc53 did not touch the directory template body; the trimPrefix-only template this finding targets is verbatim from round-0 commit b434ef7. The fix replaces it with the full home-collapse/project-relative/basename-fallback logic mirroring legacy getDisplayDirectoryName, and the agent's own reply corrects the reviewer's stated equal-case behavior after checking the legacy function directly.
guidance_note: When migrating a segment renderer to a template DSL, trace every branch of the legacy function (equal-path, outside-project, home-collapse) instead of a template that only reproduces the one fixture value in hand.

evidence: The parity harness (test/parity.test.ts) asserts DSL output byte-equal to committed golden for every dsl-parity segment, which would catch any glyph drift regardless of whether the DSL literal or SYMBOLS diverges first; per the PR's own description bzh.2 deletes the SYMBOLS indirection outright, supporting the claim that literal glyphs are the DSL's intended form rather than a second source of truth.

`gh api .../commits/3f366b3` (the fix for F3) shows it introduced the full DIR_TEMPLATE with `{{ if hasPrefix .home .current_dir }}` but no truthiness guard on `.home`; F3's own reply listed verification across relative/equal/trailing-slash/outside-project/under-home inputs but never the unset-HOME case, which is exactly the vacuous-prefix bug F5 caught next round (hasPrefix("", x) is true, collapsing every path to "~<path>").
guidance_note: When adding a legacy-mirroring guard (collapseHome's `if (home && ...)`), copy the truthiness check together with the prefix check in the same edit, and include the empty/unset case explicitly in the fix's own verification matrix.

evidence: GIT_STATUS's dirty-before-conflicts ordering is present verbatim in round-0 commit b434ef7 (confirmed via gh); dd8d1f3 (the fix for F5) only touched the HOME capture/guard, never GIT_STATUS. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation — this is a round-0 bug the reviewer caught in round 3, currently masked because the fixture never exercises status==="dirty" and status==="conflicts" simultaneously (impossible for a single enum value), but real if the enum's semantics ever change.
guidance_note: When translating a legacy if/else-if precedence chain into nested template conditionals, match the exact branch order even when current enum values make it currently equivalent.

evidence: Confirmed via gh that model's `.model.display_name` verbatim template is present since round-0 commit b434ef7, unrelated to dd8d1f3. The agent agreed formatModelName normalization is genuinely unreachable in the DSL today but chose to file it as a future ticket (bzh.5) and add a comment while leaving `model` inside this PR's dsl-parity flip — that left a live correctness gap (decorated model names would silently diverge) behind a status label asserting parity. cc-candybar#20, merged 3 minutes after this PR, had to downgrade model's status to dsl-pending to actually close the gap, confirming the comment-only response was insufficient. Citing [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] to justify deferring the fix is a stretch — that law is about representing state as data, not a license to defer a known gap.
guidance_note: When a migrated DSL segment provably diverges from legacy for real (non-fixture) inputs, downgrade its parity status to dsl-pending in the same PR that discovers the gap, rather than leaving it dsl-parity with a comment.

evidence: `HOOK_DATA.version!` with no `when` guard is present verbatim in round-0 commit b434ef7; dd8d1f3 never touched the version binding. False positive on the ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag — a round-0 gap surfaced in round 3.
guidance_note: Seed a safe default and add a `when` guard for every optional field a migrated segment's legacy renderer null-checks, in the same commit that seeds the field.

evidence: GIT_TEMPLATE's unconditional `.git.repoName` prefix is present verbatim in round-0 commit b434ef7; dd8d1f3 never touched GIT_TEMPLATE. False positive on the ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag.
guidance_note: When a legacy renderer gates a prefix on both a flag and an optional field's presence, reproduce both conditions, not just render the field unconditionally.

evidence: The git store's non-null assertions (`GIT_INFO.repoName!`, `.sha!`, `.staged!`, etc.) are present verbatim in round-0 commit b434ef7; dd8d1f3 never touched the git store block. False positive on the ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag.
guidance_note: Seed optional upstream fields with the same safe defaults (""/0) the template's own presence guards expect, instead of asserting them non-null.

evidence: The tmux binding's plain `.tmux.session` interpolation (no "none" fallback) is present verbatim in round-0 commit b434ef7; dd8d1f3 never touched the tmux binding. False positive on the ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag.
guidance_note: When a legacy renderer has an explicit fallback string for an empty/missing value (renderTmux's "tmux:none"), reproduce the fallback text, not just the interpolation.

narrative: This is the batch's clearest case of both a real fix-caused-fix chain and repeated false-positive flags. F5 (round 2, an empty-HOME vacuous-prefix bug) was genuinely introduced by F3's round-1 fix, which added HOME-collapse logic without the truthiness guard its own legacy-mirroring comment implied — an avoidable round. By contrast, all six round-3 findings (F6-F11) and two of the round-1 findings (F2, F3) carry an ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag but were verified via gh to be verbatim in the original round-0 commit, simply uncaught until later rounds — the flag correlates with 'this is the commit under review' more than with 'this fix caused this bug', and needed per-finding diffing to tell apart. Separately, F7's decision to leave `model` marked dsl-parity behind a comment rather than downgrading its status was corrected only by a follow-up PR three minutes later.
guidance_observations: Six of eleven findings in this PR were pre-existing gaps from the very first commit that Copilot simply hadn't surfaced yet — the round count here is driven mostly by the reviewer's incremental depth, not by fix quality.
The one real incomplete-fix chain (F3 to F5) happened because the fix's own stated verification matrix didn't include the exact edge case (empty HOME) that mirrors the guard it was supposed to add.

F7's 'file a ticket and add a comment' response to a real correctness gap in a segment left marked dsl-parity was under-corrective; the safer move (downgrade to dsl-pending) is what the very next PR had to do anyway.

evidence: The comment referenced a nonexistent `formatModel` function; the actual legacy normalizer is `formatModelName` in src/utils/formatters.ts. The fix corrects the comment to name the real function, a purely cosmetic but accurate correction.
guidance_note: Name the real function/file when writing a comment that references specific code, so a reader can actually find what's missing.

narrative: A tiny, targeted PR that itself functions as the correction cc-candybar#19/F7 should have made: it downgrades `model` from dsl-parity to dsl-pending so the byte-parity harness stops implicitly certifying a segment with a known normalization gap. The only review finding was a one-word factual error in the new comment, fixed immediately.
guidance_observations: This PR is the corrective action cc-candybar#19/F7 deferred to 'a future ticket' — it landed 3 minutes after #19 merged, showing the gap was live enough to need same-session follow-up rather than a filed-away ticket.
